title: ConstantStepReshuffledSmoothConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of F(x) = (1/n)∑ᵢ fᵢ(x), with every component convex and a minimizer x⋆ satisfying ‖x₀−x⋆‖ ≤ R.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: There are n ≥ 1 component functions on a complete real Hilbert space E.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Every reply is the exact component gradient, for every call index and oracle seed. There is no oracle error.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query specifies a component index i and a point x; one oracle call returns ∇fᵢ(x).

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: At a minimizer satisfying the initial-distance bound, (1/n)∑ᵢ ‖∇fᵢ(x⋆)‖² ≤ σ². This bounds component-gradient heterogeneity at that minimizer, without imposing a uniform variance bound elsewhere.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Component gradients have Lipschitz constants ℓᵢ ≥ 0 with ℓᵢ ≤ Lmax and (1/n)∑ᵢ ℓᵢ ≤ Lavg. Valid parameters satisfy 0 < Lavg ≤ Lmax, R ≥ 0, σ ≥ 0, and ε > 0. Algorithms are restricted to reshuffledGradient with a positive constant step size. All Params, including E, n, Lavg, Lmax, R, σ, ε, and x₀, are public; the component functions are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ReshuffledSmoothConvex.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/ConstantStepReshuffledSmoothConvex.lean: spec.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is the final point of the permitted constant-step reshuffledGradient algorithm. Its objective gap F(output)−F(x⋆) must be integrable and have expectation at most ε; the output must be measurable.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee is in expectation under the product of the algorithm and oracle seed laws. The oracle-call budget is fixed and bounded for every seed.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Smooth convex finite-sum optimization with exact component gradients, random reshuffling, heterogeneity measured at a minimizer, and expected objective-gap accuracy is an established formulation.

descriptionHtml:
Constant-Step Random Reshuffling

We consider minimizing F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x) on a real Hilbert space E, where n≥1 and the functions fi:E→R are differentiable and convex with Lipschitz gradients. A given point x0∈E satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R for a minimizer x⋆ of F, with n−1∑i=1n∥∇fi(x⋆)∥2≤σ2, where R,σ≥0. The oracle returns ∇fi(x) at (i,x). We analyze constant-step random reshuffling and require its last iterate x¯ to satisfy E[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, where ε>0 and the expectation is over the random permutations.

The optimization problem is minx∈EF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. Fix smoothness bounds 0<Lavg≤Lmax. The algorithm receives E, n, Lavg, Lmax, R, σ, ε, and x0; the component functions are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and smoothness). Each fi is Fréchet differentiable on E and satisfies fi((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)fi(x)+tfi(y),x,y∈E,t∈[0,1]. There exist constants ℓ1,…,ℓn such that 0≤ℓi≤Lmax,1n∑i=1nℓi≤Lavg,∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥≤ℓi∥x−y∥,x,y∈E. These conditions hold for every i∈{1,…,n}.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance and component gradients). There exists x⋆∈E such that F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,1n∑i=1n∥∇fi(x⋆)∥2≤σ2.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze constant-step random reshuffling. The algorithm chooses an integer K≥0 and a constant step size η>0 from the available inputs. It draws K independent, uniformly distributed permutations π0,…,πK−1 of {1,…,n}. For every epoch k≥K, set πk to the identity permutation. Starting from the given x0, the updates are xt+1=xt−η∇fπk(j+1)(xt),k=⌊t/n⌋,j=t−nk,t=0,1,…. Thus each of the first K epochs visits every component once in a fresh random order, and subsequent epochs use the fixed order 1,…,n. The same step size is used throughout. Each update makes one component-gradient query, which may be evaluated at any point of E.

For an allotted number N≥0 of oracle calls, the output is the last iterate x¯=xN, including when the calls end partway through an epoch. Let P be the law of the sampled permutations. The output must be measurable, its objective gap must be integrable under P, and it must satisfy EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
On a real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, let F=n−1∑i=1nfi, n≥1, with convex fi and Li-Lipschitz gradients, 0≤Li≤Lmax and n−1∑iLi≤Lavg≤Lmax, Lavg>0. A minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and n−1∑i∥∇fi(x⋆)∥2≤σ2, where R,σ≥0. The setup requires constant positive-step reshuffling; each epoch uses a fresh independent uniform permutation and exact component gradients. The target is ∫[F(xnK(ω))−F(x⋆)]dP(ω)≤ε, ε>0, for the measurable raw final iterate and its integrable gap. Costs count all component-gradient calls. Prior-work comparisons below are on the common Euclidean case E=Rd; alternative methods need not satisfy the setup’s algorithm restriction.

Constant-step random reshuffling: ConstantStepReshuffledSmoothConvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) ReshuffledConstantStepLastIterate (Ours) (review) O(n+(u+s)H)
(2) VRADA (Song et al. 2021, Theorem 1); unregularized case O(n[1+log⁡(1+log⁡n)]+nu) (1): O(n) versus O(n[1+log⁡(1+log⁡n)]) when (u+s)H≲n; at most a double-logarithmic saving for expected objective accuracy. (1) needs σ; worse when u≫n or s≫n+nu, potentially polynomially.
(3) IID SGD (Attia et al. 2025, Theorem 2); uniform component sampling O(1+(u+s)log⁡(2+u+s)) (1): No established improvement over this raw-last-iterate guarantee. (1) pays a full-epoch cost n, worse when n≫1+(u+s)log⁡(2+u+s); requires reshuffling instead of IID draws.
(4) RR (Liu and Zhou 2024, Theorem 4.4, Appendix C.1); ψ=0 O(n+nqlog⁡(2+q)) (1): deterministic-term saving at least nLavg/Lmax/H when this ratio is large. Noise-term saving if ε≫σ2H2/(nLavg); method-specific gains. (1) loses Lavg sensitivity; worse noise term when sH≫blog⁡(2+q).
(5) RR (Liu 2026, Theorem 1, Corollary 1); averaged output O(n+u+min{s,b}) (1): raw last iterate instead of averaging all inner iterates; a multi-epoch constant-step RR guarantee. (1) pays factor H and loses the smaller noise branch when ε<σ2/(nLavg); logarithmically smaller step cap.

Abbr: RR: random reshuffling; IID: independent identically distributed; P: law of the algorithm’s permutations; K: epochs; u=LmaxR2/ε, s=σ2R2/ε2, H=(1+log⁡n)[1+log⁡(n+2+u+s)]; b=nLavgσR2/ε3/2; q=LavgLmaxR2/ε+b/n. All logarithms are natural; ≲ suppresses universal constants.

Liu, Zijian. 2026. Random Reshuffling Dominates Stochastic Gradient Descent. arXiv:2606.32005v1. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2606.32005.

import LongTails.Setups.ReshuffledSmoothConvex

namespace LongTails.Setups.ConstantStepReshuffledSmoothConvex

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Params := LongTails.Setups.ReshuffledSmoothConvex.Params

abbrev spec : Setup :=
  { LongTails.Setups.ReshuffledSmoothConvex.spec with
    allowedAlgorithm := fun q algorithm =>
      ∃ (K : ℕ) (η : ℝ), 0 < η ∧ algorithm =
        ReshuffledConvex.reshuffledGradient K (fun _ => η) q.x0 }

end LongTails.Setups.ConstantStepReshuffledSmoothConvex
